full_judgment:
Plaintiffs case in short is that the land in suit and some other land belonged to his father and the same was requisitioned in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51, that the land in suit measuring .13 acre has been leased out on October 14, 1984 to him by the Ministry of Works for 99 years and thereupon he got the land recorded in his name and paying rent, that he has erected pukka latrine and transplanted trees and is enjoying the land so leased out to him, that he has applied to the House Building Finance Corporation for loan to build a 4 stored building and that he has started foundation work, that on June 2, 1987 defendants threatened him to dispossess from the land in suit, although defendants have no right, title, possession and interest in the land in suit and that paper on the basis of which defendants have raised claim are not genuine and the same are only paper transactions and as such he has been constrained to file the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint. Their case, amongst others, is that the land in suit along with other land was requisitioned for the use of Dhaka Railway Station and yard and the land so acquired for use of the Railway Station and yard was handed over to Railway on December 19, 1965 and February 27, 1966, that plaintiff has not obtained any lease of the land in suit from the Ministry of Works, that the land in suit is being used by the Railway as its yard and the materials of the Railway have been stacked there, that plaintiff has filed the suit with the end in view to enjoy Railway's land illegally, that the land in suit was acquired in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51 for Dhaka Railway Station and its yard, that the Ministry of Works by its letter dated March 22, 1984 has informed the Railway that the said Ministry never leased out the suit land for 99 years to the plaintiff, that the land in suit is in the possession of the Railway. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of the appellant that the High Court Division was in error in not noticing that the suit so filed was barred because of the provision of Section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 as the land in suit was acquired for the Railway in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51, that the land in suit along with other land was acquired for Railway and possession of the land so acquired in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51 was handed over to the Railway on December 19, 1965 and February 27, 1966 and the Railway is possessing the same as Station and yard and the Railway being the requiring body, the Ministry of Works had no right to lease out the land in suit to the plaintiff and the alleged transfer was made by the Ministry of Works beyond its power and as such the transfer, if any, has been made is void and thus High Court Division was in error in holding that the plaintiff has title and possession of the land in suit, that in a suit for permanent injunction the Court is required to discuss the question of exclusive possession of the plaintiff, but the High Court Division as well as the Court of appeal below did not give any finding as to the question of exclusive possession of the plaintiff. 

 7. It is the case of the plaintiff that the land in suit and other belonged to his father and the same was requisitioned in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51 and that out of the land so requisitioned in the aforesaid L.A. case the Ministry of Works has leased out the land in suit i.e. .13 acre of land to him on October 14, 1984 and since then he upon getting the land recorded in his name paying rent and is in possession of the land in suit and he has erected structures and also has planted trees in the land in suit. 

 8. As against the aforesaid case of the plaintiff, the case of the defendant is that the land in suit along with the other land was acquired in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51 for Railway Station and yard and the possession of the land so acquired was handed over to the Railway on December 19, 1965 and February 27, 1966 and since then Railway is possessing the same and using the same for the purpose for which the land in suit kind other land was acquired and that although plaintiff is claiming the land in suit on the alleged basis of lease from the Ministry of works, but the said Ministry by its letter dated March 22, 1984 has informed the Railway that it has never leased out the land in suit for 99 years to the plaintiff. It is also the case of the Railway that the plaintiff has filed the suit to grab the land of the Railway. 

 10. In the background of their aforesaid case we are of the view the parties, particularly the Railway, were to get the land relayed with reference to the paper filed by the Railway in assertion of the claim the land in suit along with the other land was handed over to the Railway. It may be mentioned the Railway filed the letter and a map which has compositely been marked as Ext-B. At one stage of the hearing of the appeal we called for the record of the Title Suit No.563 of 1987 of the 4th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka and upon examination of the record we noticed that the Railway to establish its claim that the land in suit and the other land acquired in L.A. Case No.4 of 1950-51 was handed over to it for Railway Station and its yard filed a map bearing joint signatures of the acquiring body and requiring body.
